label: REVISED VISION PROMPT · exam clip 04:55-06:00 · findings register
source_media: knee-exam-clip.mp4 (65s cut from knee-visit-CORRECT-ORDER.mp4 at 04:55, contains the whole physical exam)
prompt_variant: Prompt Studio 'Vision - findings register (test)' v1, job=vision_frame, published to ALL on dev 2026-08-16. REPLACES VISION_GROUNDED_SYSTEM_PROMPT at runtime.

experiment.question: Is the vision layer's literalism a prompt artefact or a modality limit?
experiment.control: Same footage under the shipped prompt — see run 2026-08-16T17-05 (session 30cccd75, clip bb7dabb1 which contains this 65s window).
experiment.result: BOTH. Register improved measurably; manoeuvre naming did not. The two hypotheses are independent and both were correct.

measured.register_shift: PASS — captions now name examination techniques (bimanual palpation, range-of-motion assessment), anatomical landmarks (joint line, popliteal fossa, peripatellar region) and give degree estimates. Zero degree estimates appeared under the old prompt.
measured.named_manoeuvres: 0 of 7 — Lachman 0, McMurray 0, milking 0, sweep 0, patellar grind 0, patellar mobility 0. Unchanged.
measured.scar_fabrication: GONE. 'scar' occurs 0 times. It had reproduced on two prior sessions under the shipped prompt; the added grounding clause ('Every finding must be supported by what is actually visible in this frame') is the only change that could account for it.

experiment.model_states_the_limit_itself: The manoeuvre cannot be definitively classified from this frame.
experiment.caveat: Degree estimates ('approximately 20-30 degrees') are judgements from a photograph. Ranges rather than false precision is the right behaviour, but whether the angles are ACCURATE needs a clinician's read, not mine.
